pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 4.5.1 NARRATIVE AND DESCRIPTIVE PARAGRAPHS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.5: Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can we make a narrative composition interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. write narrative and descriptive paragraphs
2. use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs
3. value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs

Teach
• Focus skill: write narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we make a narrative composition interesting?
2. How can we ensure unity in a paragraph?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
